result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers propose similar Free, Personal, Family and Pro plans that cover all three groups. A's cost arithmetic checks out throughout and it frames every price as a starting point to test. B overstates Family search costs, saying 300 searches cost $1.80 when they cost $0.90. B also brings in competitor prices (Google and Dropbox) and frames its prices less clearly as tests. B does add useful caveats about bandwidth and app-store fees, and gives a cleaner feature matrix. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B's arithmetic is correct throughout, including caps, blocks and margins, and it presents every price as a range to test without making up competitor figures.
